title: RBAC final cutover — production checklist
description: Machine-readable twin of docs/architecture/RBAC_CUTOVER.md. Nothing in this repository executes it against production; every step marked requires_approval needs the named approval first.
preconditions: the release containing RBAC-8 is built and its test suites are green
a DBA/operator has approved the production cutover (record the reference)
a maintenance window is agreed: during steps 4–12 the application is restarted once

steps.title: Take a full database dump
steps.verify: a new backups/*_full.dump exists and pg_restore -l lists its tables

steps.title: Read-only readiness and reconciliation report
steps.verify: reviewed: how many accounts would be assigned; unmapped_legacy and no_legacy_role lists understood

steps.title: Apply the schema (additive; users.role_id becomes nullable)
steps.command: python -m scripts.rbac.cutover apply --allow-database ccure_db --production-approved <REF>   (runs steps schema…verify)
steps.verify: alembic current shows the new head; rbac_* tables exist
steps.rollback: alembic downgrade c9e3a7b5d1f2@-1 (only while every account still has a legacy role)

steps.title: Sync the permission catalogue and system roles
steps.verify: readiness: no missing declared permission, five system roles present
steps.rollback: catalogue rows are additive; nothing to undo

steps.title: Assign every active account the RBAC role its legacy role maps to
steps.verify: readiness: no missing or incorrect assignment; unmapped accounts listed
steps.rollback: assignments are revoked, never deleted, through RBAC administration

steps.title: Verify a privileged administrator exists
steps.command: python -m scripts.rbac.cutover verify   (and, if none: python -m scripts.rbac.bootstrap_admin --email … --reason … --allow-database ccure_db --production-approved <REF>)

steps.title: Self-registration default role
steps.verify: readiness note absent: the default role is the read-only system role

steps.title: Every active organisation has an account able to assign roles
Deploy the release (RBAC is authoritative in this code; there is no switch)
steps.command: docker compose up -d --no-deps api  (after the image/volume carries the release)
steps.verify: api healthy; no 'RBAC catalogue could not be applied' CRITICAL line in docker logs
steps.rollback: redeploy the previous release after `cutover rollback-prepare --apply`

steps.title: Smoke tests
steps.command: sign in as an administrator, an organisation administrator, an analyst and a viewer
steps.verify: /auth/me shows each account's permissions; GET /platform/rbac/roles works for the administrator; a viewer is refused POST /scan/host-discovery; an organisation administrator cannot see another organisation; the frontend shows the Platform RBAC administration page

steps.title: Audit verification
steps.verify: one rbac.role.assigned event per provisioned account; rbac.bootstrap.administrator if bootstrap ran

steps.title: Legacy authorization status
steps.verify: no code reads users.role_id, roles, permissions or role_permissions for authorization (tests/repo/test_rbac_final_ratchet.py); the tables are retained, non-authoritative

steps.title: Rollback (only if smoke tests fail)
steps.command: python -m scripts.rbac.cutover rollback-prepare --apply --allow-database ccure_db --production-approved <REF>; redeploy the previous release; restore the dump only if data was damaged
steps.verify: previous release signs in and authorizes from users.role_id again
